answer: A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own zephyr path. Since the delta verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator forfeits a fresh proof per key, and the timber audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 31 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 34 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
